title: Time complexity and space complexity fundamentals
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its constraints.
Trace the example and reason about its data flow.
Identify complexity, boundary or safety considerations.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Time complexity describes how an algorithm's work grows with input size; space complexity describes how its memory use grows. Big-O notation expresses an asymptotic upper-bound classification and commonly helps compare growth rates.
understand.whyItMatters: Complexity analysis helps choose algorithms that remain practical as input sizes increase, but real performance also depends on constants, memory access, compiler and hardware.
understand.analogy: Treat an algorithm or data structure as a set of operations that must preserve a clearly stated contract.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace formal complexity analysis, C object rules or algorithm preconditions.

explain.narrative:
Time complexity describes how an algorithm's work grows with input size; space complexity describes how its memory use grows. Big-O notation expresses an asymptotic upper-bound classification and commonly helps compare growth rates.

Before implementation, state input constraints, empty-case behaviour, ownership and invariants. Compile with warnings and test representative, boundary and failure cases.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: In the worst case, contains examines every element, so its time grows linearly with count: O(n). It uses a fixed amount of additional storage, O(1).

practise.guidedTask: Count the maximum comparisons for arrays of lengths 5 and 100.
practise.independentTask: Compare linear search and binary search, stating the preconditions for binary search and the time/space trade-offs.
hints: State whether you are discussing best, average or worst case.
Binary search requires the input to be sorted under the comparison being used.
Big-O describes growth, not an exact runtime in seconds.
